claims.text: Hallucination in large language models can be formulated as geometric overflow.
Geometric overflow is defined as boundary violation under preserved internal coherence.
In the geometric overflow failure regime, outputs remain fluent.
In the geometric overflow failure regime, outputs remain internally stable.
In the geometric overflow failure regime, outputs remain high-confidence.
In the geometric overflow failure regime, outputs violate externally defined constraints.
Boundary tension is a geometric quantity that measures proximity to admissibility boundaries.
Boundary tension enables the detection of limit-state behavior preceding overflow.
Geometric overflow is orthogonal to model calibration.
Perfectly calibrated models may exhibit coherent boundary crossing.
Regime separability exists between overflow and collapse in retrieval-augmented question answering settings.

evidence.description: The authors provide a proof that overflow is orthogonal to calibration.
The paper proves that even perfectly calibrated models may exhibit coherent boundary crossing.
A minimal empirical illustration in a retrieval-augmented question answering setting demonstrates regime separability between overflow and collapse.

methodologies.name: Geometric Overflow Formulation
methodologies.description: A boundary-based formulation of hallucination defining an admissible manifold induced by a structured family of constraints grounded in an external environment.

methodologies.name: Boundary Tension Measurement
methodologies.description: A geometric quantity measuring proximity to admissibility boundaries to detect limit-state behavior.

limitations.text: Existing perspectives like probabilistic miscalibration, distributional shift, or generalization error do not explicitly distinguish between internal representational instability and externally grounded boundary violations.

future_work.text: Development of boundary-aware diagnostics for LLMs.
